title: Variations in root functional traits facilitate the adaptation of pioneer plants to rare earth element mine tailings
content:
Our findings highlight the pivotal role of root chemical traits and intraspecific plasticity in facilitating the adaptation of pioneer plants to extreme REE tailing environments. The observed shifts towards stress-tolerant ‘slow’ strategies and ‘do-it-yourself’ nutrient acquisition provide a trait-based framework for advancing phytoremediation in the ecological restoration of degraded mine tailings, such as informing plant species selection.


Abstract

The trade-offs in plant root traits significantly influence the adaptation and community dynamics in heterogeneous habitats. However, the role of inter- and intraspecific root trait variation in the adaptation of pioneer plants in stressed mine tailings is poorly understood. We assessed root morphological and chemical traits of 16 dominant species from unexploited forest sites adjacent to rare earth elements (REEs) mine tailings, and three pioneer species (Miscanthus sinensis, Dicranopteris linearis and Pinus massoniana) across a gradient of soil stress—including REEs toxicity, nutrient deficiency and compaction—from forest to REEs tailings. In the two-dimensional root economics space (RES), the contents of cellulose, hemicellulose and silicon were coaxial with the collaboration gradients (‘do-it-yourself’–‘outsourcing’) and inversely related to fine root diameter. Meanwhile, root REEs content aligned with conservation gradients (‘fast’–‘slow’), indicating a slow strategy. Interspecific variations did not show a distinct strategy preference for pioneer species compared with non-pioneer plants. However, notable intraspecific variations were observed, particularly in stress-related traits, such as root N content, C:N ratio and REEs content, which exceeded interspecific variations. All three pioneer species exhibited a shift towards ‘slow’ strategies, while P. massoniana also transitioned towards ‘do-it-yourself’ strategies, driven by increased soil bulk density, elevated bioavailable REEs content, and reduced soil carbon and nutrient levels in the tailings. Synthesis and applications. Our findings highlight the pivotal role of root chemical traits and intraspecific plasticity in facilitating the adaptation of pioneer plants to extreme REE tailing environments. The observed shifts towards stress-tolerant ‘slow’ strategies and ‘do-it-yourself’ nutrient acquisition provide a trait-based framework for advancing phytoremediation in the ecological restoration of degraded mine tailings, such as informing plant species selection.

摘要

植物根系性状间的权衡关系显著影响不同生境中的个体适应性与群落动态。然而，在受胁迫尾矿环境中，种间与种内根系性状变异对先锋植物适应的作用机制仍有待阐明。 本研究选取了稀土尾矿附近未开采林地中的16个优势物种，以及从林地至稀土尾矿地沿土壤胁迫(包含稀土毒性、养分匮乏及土壤板结)梯度分布的三种先锋植物(芒草、芒萁、马尾松)，分析其根系形态与化学性状。 在二维根系经济空间中，纤维素、半纤维素和硅含量与协作梯度(“自主”-“外包”)同轴分布，且与细根直径呈负相关。同时，根系稀土含量沿保守梯度(“快速”-“慢速”)分布，指示慢速策略。 与非先锋植物相比，先锋植物的种间差异未呈现明显的策略偏好。但种内变异尤为显著，其中根系氮含量、碳氮比及稀土含量等胁迫适应相关性状的变异程度甚至超过了种间差异。受尾矿区土壤容重增加、生物有效态稀土含量升高及土壤碳和养分水平下降的驱动，三种先锋植物均向“慢速”策略变化，而马尾松还表现出向“自主”策略的偏移。 综合应用:本研究揭示了根系化学性状与种内可塑性在先锋植物适应极端稀土尾矿环境中的关键作用。研究观察到，这些植物的根系倾向于往耐胁迫“慢速”策略与“自主”养分获取策略转变。这一发现为推进基于性状的植物修复技术提供了理论框架，对退化尾矿地的生态恢复实践，如植物物种的筛选，具有重要指导意义。
